uncited: Image-Based Volumetric Shadows is a screen-space technique that approximates volumetric shadowing by leveraging geometric depth information and image-based processing, avoiding the computational cost of full ray marching through participating media.

Unlike parent method [Soft BiF Volumetric Shadows](18810-soft-bif-volumetric-shadows.md) which relies on spatial interpolation of sampled radiance, this approach uses epipolar geometry, bilateral filtering, and depth discontinuities to determine shadowing along view rays.

It is distinct from geometric-based methods [Geometrical-Based Volumetric Shadows](18811-geometrical-based-volumetric-shadows.md) by replacing explicit polygon casting or depth peeling with image-space operations such as downsampling and rectification.
The method is not a single algorithm but a family of screen-space techniques that share the goal of computing volumetric shadows using image-based primitives.
Implementations vary by author, but all operate in screen space using depth buffers and epipolar lines.
- **Downsampled Buffer**: Lower-resolution representation of shadow/scattering state.
- **Epipolar Line Data**: Linear arrays of samples along epipolar lines in screen space.
The general workflow involves placing samples along epipolar lines, detecting depth discontinuities, and applying filtering.
The following pseudocode represents a generalized implementation based on Tóth and Engelhardt, as no single source provides a complete unified algorithm.
- **Filter Radius**: Not given in the sources.
- **Downsampling Factor**: Not given in the sources.
- **Discontinuity Threshold**: Not given in the sources.
- **Time Complexity**: Depends on the number of samples per pixel and filter radius.
Generally faster than ray marching due to screen-space operations.
- **Memory Complexity**: Requires depth buffer and intermediate buffers for downsampling and filtering.
- **Limitations**: Screen-space only (no off-screen shadows), artifacts at depth discontinuities, dependent on depth buffer accuracy.
- **When to Use**: Real-time applications where performance is critical and screen-space shadows are sufficient.
- **When Not to Use**: When off-screen shadows are required or when high-quality volumetric scattering is needed.
